sections.h2: Three ways to sell in Allen
sections.html:
Owners in Allen can hire a broker, locate a buyer without one, or accept cash from an investor. Let the condition of the house and your own deadline decide. Allen is in the southwest corner of Collin County next to U.S. 75, with an estimated 113,447 residents in mid-2025.

Roughly seven in ten occupied homes here belong to the people living in them, which means a clean, updated house attracts many move-in buyers. A house that needs work, carries a lease, or sits in probate is easier to place with someone who takes it as it is and follows your calendar.

  • Brokered listing: the most buyers see it, but expect showings, loan approvals and inspection haggling.
  • Private sale: you set the number, show the house and handle the contract on your own.
  • Cash purchase: one buyer, no repair work for you, and a closing date you choose.

Allen is an affluent suburb with a strong owner base. Its count rose from 84,246 in 2010 to 104,627 in 2020, roughly 20,000 new residents.

Landlords selling an Allen property should read this first. The council voted on October 13 to make single-family rentals (houses, townhomes and duplexes) register with the city and submit to inspection.

  • Yearly fee: $150, plus $50 if you register late.
  • A follow-up inspection for continuing problems costs $25.
  • Mailings to owners were scheduled to begin in November 2026, and registration is first due January 31, 2027.
  • Rentals of this type are about 14% of the city's housing yet caused 38% of property violations, hence the exterior inspections.

City staff are matching ownership data against utility accounts to find rentals. If a notice arrives for a home that was never leased, the notice tells you how to contact the city. If guests ever paid to stay overnight, ask permitting staff whether a permit was issued.

Remodel and repair permits run through the Building and Permitting Division. Request the permit history for your address, because a file a former owner left open can stall a closing.

Two Collin County bodies split the work. The appraisal district (Collin CAD) decides what your house is worth, and the county tax assessor-collector bills and collects. Bills arrive in October, and January 31 is the last day to pay without penalty. Tax certificates and similar special requests are handled only at the Property Tax Office, 2300 Bloomdale Road, Suite 2324, McKinney.

Exemption forms go to the appraisal district, not the tax office. The district accepts the standard homestead form from January 1 to April 30 only, and it charges nothing and will not take it by email. A late filing can still be made within two years of the bill going delinquent.

The district's 2023 table showed these entries for Allen city. The district posts a new table every year, so look up current figures first.

  • Homestead: 5.00% of value, but never under $5,000.
  • Owners 65 or older: $50,000.
  • Disabled owners: $25,000.

Sellers who are 65 or older and have a school tax ceiling can transfer it to a replacement Texas home as a percentage. Your buyer must file a new homestead application in their own name.

The Collin County Clerk records every Allen deed. Bring the original, or a certified copy from the clerk, with signatures notarized. Some entries online are redacted under House Bill 4350, and that site is not the official repository, so rely on the clerk's office for the actual record.

Before recording, Texas needs the signer's acknowledgment in front of a notary or similar officer, or a witness. Charges vary by document and shift over the years, so ask the clerk what the current schedule is.

Normally the title company runs the process: it orders the tax certificate, pays the mortgage off and sends the deed in. Because each tax year's lien attaches on January 1, any earlier year still owing must be paid before the transfer is clean.

sections.h2: Inherited, behind on payments or rented?
sections.html:
Each of these has its own deadline under Texas law.

  • Inherited house: the window to probate a will runs four years from the death. If the estate needs no administration, heirs can convey with a muniment of title, supported by the court order and the will recorded in the county that holds the land.
  • Mortgage trouble: after a default letter you have 20 days to catch up, then the lender must post a sale notice at least 21 days before the auction.
  • Tenants in place: a lease may set its own terms, but the default is a written three-day notice to vacate, then a case in justice court.

Closing first, before the auction date or the eviction hearing, leaves the decisions with you instead of the lender or the court.

An investor paying cash needs no appraisal and no loan approval, so those waiting periods drop away. Staging, weekend open houses and post-inspection repair demands drop away too. Only the title work is left: the tax certificate, any mortgage payoff, and the deed.

If the house was a rental, say up front whether the tenants will remain and whether registration is current. Buyers factor that into the price, and a problem found at the last minute costs more than one disclosed early.

sections.h2: From signed contract to closing day
sections.html:
When a contract is signed, a title company starts the file. Its staff request the tax certificate in McKinney, ask each lender for a payoff letter, and comb the records for liens and permits that were never closed. At the table you sign the deed before a notary. Once funds move, the deed is sent to the county clerk, and the appraisal district later changes the owner of record to match.

Delays typically come from an overlooked tax balance or an old open permit. Ask for both the same week you accept an offer so the closing date holds.

Collect these in writing.

  • A tax certificate showing nothing owed for earlier years.
  • Proof from Collin CAD that your homestead and any ceiling are on record.
  • If it was a rental, the city's registration record for the address.
  • A title search covering open permits and liens not yet released.
  • The closing date and who pays which closing costs, stated in the contract.

Have the title company quote a payoff for each lien, and keep a copy of every certificate. Paperwork on hand when the buyer's side asks means a faster close.

faqs.q: Does Allen require rental houses to be registered?
faqs.a: Single-family rentals must register, whether houses, townhomes or duplexes, and they are subject to inspection. The yearly fee is $150 with $50 added for late registration, and the first deadline is January 31, 2027.

faqs.q: Who collects property tax on an Allen home?
faqs.a: The county's tax assessor-collector, whose office is in McKinney. Values and exemptions come from Collin Central Appraisal District.

faqs.q: When can I apply for a homestead exemption on an Allen house?
faqs.a: January 1 through April 30, filed with Collin CAD, free of charge. Forms sent early or by email are turned away. A late filing is possible for two years after the account goes delinquent.

faqs.q: Can I sell an Allen house if property taxes are unpaid?
faqs.a: Yes. Whatever is owed gets paid from your proceeds at closing, because the lien dated January 1 stays with the house and blocks clear title until it is cleared.

faqs.q: How many people live in Allen?
faqs.a: An estimated 113,447 in mid-2025, compared with 104,627 at the 2020 count.
